assertions.subject: DDX39B-targeting siRNA DDX_4
assertions.source_locator: Fig1A,E,F; Methods DDX39B RNAi-mediated knockdown and rescue
assertions.evidence_summary: DDX39B siRNA depletion was verified by western blot; rescue experiment used DDX_4 targeting endogenous 3-prime UTR absent from the rescue cDNA.
assertions.duration: siRNA days1,3,5; harvest day9 in rescue
assertions.assay: western blot anti-DDX39B ab47955, hnRNPA1 loading control
assertions.causal_directness: Direct depletion verified at protein layer; transgene bypasses targeted UTR.
assertions.limitations: HeLa transformed cells; siRNA depletion differs in magnitude/mechanism from inherited rs2523506 allele.

assertions.subject: siRNA-resistant wild-type DDX39B complementation
assertions.source_locator: Fig1E,F; Results first subsection; Methods DDX39B RNAi-mediated knockdown and rescue
assertions.evidence_summary: Wild-type DDX39B cDNA rescued endogenous IL7R exon6 splicing in depleted HeLa cells; helicase-defective D199A did not.
assertions.stimulation: DDX_4 knockdown with inducible WT or D199A transgene
assertions.assay: western blot and exon5/exon7 RT-PCR
assertions.causal_directness: Intermediate complementation supports DDX39B-dependent splice phenotype and requirement for intact helicase activity in this assay.
assertions.limitations: No primary immune-cell rescue; no direct DDX39B-RNA binding conclusion; endogenous total IL7R abundance also rises at late depletion times.
assertions.quantitative_result: At least two repeat rescue experiments; numerical rescue estimate unavailable.

assertions.subject: DDX39B sh3/sh5 depletion
assertions.source_locator: Fig6; Methods primary human CD4 culture and transduction
assertions.evidence_summary: Both shRNAs increased exon6 skipping in the six-donor activated primary CD4 panel; DDX39B protein depletion was monitored per donor.
assertions.dose: anti-CD3 50 ng/mL; anti-CD28 100 ng/mL; IL2 100 ng/mL; puromycin 1.5 microgram/mL
assertions.duration: 48 h preactivation; 72 h transduction; 96 h selection; final24 h without IL2/puromycin
assertions.assay: RT-PCR exon5/exon7; DDX39B western blot
assertions.genomic_background: rs6897932 CC or CT; no TT
assertions.causal_directness: Trans-factor perturbation; no allele edit.
assertions.limitations: Six donors, variable depletion; exact sample harvesting calendar not over-interpreted.

assertions.subject: DDX39B sh3/sh5 depletion
assertions.source_locator: Results accompanying Fig6; FigS10 caption; Methods transduction and ELISA
assertions.evidence_summary: sh3 increased supernatant IL7R in all six donors; sh5 increased it in only two despite exon-skipping changes. Authors explicitly note antibody detects all IL7R isoforms.
assertions.stimulation: same activated CD4 shRNA protocol as MG-A003
assertions.duration: final24-h collection without IL2/puromycin after transduction/selection
assertions.assay: concentrated culture-supernatant ELISA: MAB306 capture, BAF306 detection, IL7R-Fc standard
assertions.causal_directness: Protein endpoint under shared intervention; not splice-product-specific mediation.
assertions.limitations: ELISA cannot identify exon6-skipped origin; sh5 discordance unexplained; donor-matched protocol does not establish serial RNA→protein causation.

assertions.subject: rs2523506 A versus C in DDX39B 5-prime UTR
assertions.source_locator: Fig4; Methods Luciferase translation efficiency assays
assertions.evidence_summary: A-allele UTR reporters produced about20–30% lower normalized luciferase activity per reporter RNA; lysates measured24 h after transfection; RNA came from independent wells.
assertions.dose: 25 ng UTR-Renilla reporter +10 ng Firefly control per24-well
assertions.assay: dual-luciferase and RT-qPCR, Renilla/Firefly normalization then activity/RNA
assertions.causal_directness: Direct UTR allele reporter manipulation.
assertions.limitations: Reporter ORF is luciferase, not DDX39B; RNA/protein not same well; native primary-cell translation not directly measured.

assertions.subject: rs2523506 genotype
assertions.source_locator: Fig3B left; Methods DNA and RNA collection from human PBMC and LCL
assertions.evidence_summary: No detected genotype difference in DDX39B RNA in n=86 blood-derived samples labeled PBMC in the Results; Methods reveal whole-blood and additional PBMC preparations.
assertions.assay: GAPDH-normalized RT-qPCR; technical triplicates
assertions.causal_directness: Genotype association null.
assertions.limitations: Preparation per sample, disease/treatment distribution and equivalence bounds unavailable; cannot label entire cohort purified PBMC.
assertions.candidate_correction: GCO08/G-A010 preparation needs whole-blood/PBMC caveat; frozen records unchanged.

assertions.subject: rs6897932 C versus T in IL7R minigene
assertions.source_locator: Fig2b; Results differential splicing; Methods analysis of exon6 inclusion
assertions.evidence_summary: C-allele minigenes gave approximately twofold greater exon6 skipping than T in the reported assays; the human HeLa component is retained separately from rat DT3/AT3.
assertions.assay: stable minigene transfection, RT-PCR
assertions.effect_size: approximately twofold, reported Results across minigene assays; no human-only numerical value extracted
assertions.causal_directness: Allele-specific construct manipulation in HeLa.
assertions.limitations: Stable transfection endpoint timing unavailable; transient48 h timing belongs Fig2c. No protein measurement in this experiment.

assertions.subject: rs6897932 C carriage
assertions.source_locator: Results allele-specific expression; Methods allele-specific IL7R isoform expression
assertions.evidence_summary: Among94 healthy controls, C carriage associated with lower exon6–7 amplicon expression; exon4–5 and exon7–8 control amplicons did not differ significantly by genotype.
assertions.assay: TaqMan qPCR Hs00904814_m1; control junction assays Hs00233682_m1 and Hs00902338_g1
assertions.causal_directness: Genotype-associated splice-sensitive RNA endpoint.
assertions.limitations: Membrane and soluble protein statements in text are inferred from RNA; no same-panel protein measure verified.

assertions.subject: DDX39B RNA at2 h or24 h LPS
assertions.source_locator: Results sIL7R regulated by rs6897932 and associated with DDX39A; Fig3 and Supplementary Fig7
assertions.evidence_summary: All three DDX39B/BAT1 microarray probes showed no detected association with supernatant IL7R for2-h or24-h LPS RNA; all P>0.1. Total IL7R transcript also did not associate with soluble protein.

assertions.duration: RNA2 h and24 h; supernatant24 h
assertions.assay: pre-existing microarray + ELISA
assertions.causal_directness: Paired donor-data association, no regulator perturbation.

assertions.subject: rs2523506-by-rs6897932 genotype interaction
assertions.source_locator: Results after Fig3; Supplementary Fig6 referenced

assertions.ancestry: European, from explicitly reused Fairfax cohort
assertions.assay: ELISA and genotype interaction analysis
assertions.causal_directness: Candidate interaction association null.

assertions.subject: DDX39A RNA abundance after24 h LPS
assertions.source_locator: Fig3c; Results sIL7R subsection
assertions.evidence_summary: Higher DDX39A transcript abundance correlated with lower24-h monocyte supernatant IL7R in reused donor samples.

assertions.subject: CD81 TSS-directed ZIM3-dCas9 CRISPRi
assertions.source_locator: Fig1D; Results implementation; Methods gRNA transduction
assertions.evidence_summary: CD81 TSS-directed CRISPRi reduced target RNA by scRNA-seq11 days after guide transduction; two CD81 guides analyzed together due to sequence similarity.
assertions.cell_state: CD3/CD28 activated, lentivirally transduced and antibiotic-selected
assertions.stimulation: CD3/CD28 reactivation; CD81 TSS guide versus non-targeting
assertions.assay: 10X3-prime scRNA-seq

assertions.subject: CD81 TSS-directed ZIM3-dCas9 CRISPRi
assertions.source_locator: Fig1B,C; Methods gRNA transduction and flow
assertions.evidence_summary: Four-donor flow time course showed reduced cells retaining surface CD81 after TSS repression at days4,6,8,11.
assertions.cell_state: CD3/CD28 activated, lentivirally transduced and antibiotic-selected
assertions.stimulation: CD3/CD28 reactivation; CD81 TSS guide versus non-targeting
assertions.assay: flow cytometry APC anti-human CD81 clone5A6;30000–50000 events
assertions.causal_directness: Regulatory perturbation with direct surface-protein endpoint.

assertions.subject: PHF19-upstream enhancer CRISPRi
assertions.source_locator: Fig6E–H; Results primary T-cell crisprQTL helps interrogate disease-associated loci; Methods pooled screen and GWAS intersections
assertions.evidence_summary: Perturbation of the enhancer upstream of PHF19 identified TRAF1 as a differential transcript in primary CD4 cells. The region overlaps an RA credible set; paper's separate colocalization analysis supports RA risk with increased TRAF1 RNA.
assertions.cell_state: activated and expanded primary CD4 cells
assertions.dose: bead:cell1:1; pooled guide MOI<0.3; IL2 15 ng/mL
assertions.duration: fresh screen harvested10 days after transduction; second run reused cryopreserved cells then3-day recovery per sequencing Methods
assertions.assay: 10X scRNA-seq; targeted region defined by source PHF19 enhancer label
assertions.time_point: screen endpoint; see protocol discrepancy note
assertions.causal_directness: Element perturbation supports element→RNA, not exact causal SNP or protein.
assertions.limitations: Precise enhancer genomic coordinates and individual guide counts not recovered; direction of perturbation numeric effect not extracted from figure; scRNA tests showed inflated null P values and authors used multiple-guide tiers. Methods also describe2+4+6 days culture; calendar discrepancy retained.

assertions.subject: KCNN4 enhancer CRISPR deletion
assertions.source_locator: Fig5D; Results orthogonal validation; Methods CRISPR-deletions
assertions.evidence_summary: KCNN4 RNA was lower in both donor cultures after enhancer deletion, but the bulk-RNA-seq difference did not reach significance.
assertions.cell_state: activated and expanded primary CD4 cells
assertions.stimulation: CD3/CD28 then enhancer Cas9 RNP editing
assertions.dose: 1:1 bead:cell;143 pmol gRNA +47 pmol Cas9 per2 million cells
assertions.duration: edit72 h after activation; harvest10 days after editing
assertions.assay: PCR/TapeStation deletion confirmation + bulk RNA-seq
assertions.causal_directness: Orthogonal deletion validation with nonsignificant downstream RNA endpoint.

assertions.subject: rs2523506 A carriage
assertions.source_locator: Fig3C; Results allele-specific DDX39B protein; Methods DDX39B western blot analyses in LCLs
assertions.evidence_summary: Newly assayed African LCLs showed about25% lower DDX39B in AC and50% lower in AA versus CC; IBS effect was smaller and significant for CC versus AA. RNA did not differ detectably by genotype.

assertions.causal_directness: Genotype-associated native protein, not native allele replacement.
assertions.limitations: LCLs transformed and not primary CD4 cells; small AA groups; historical CEU proteomic panel had null association; exact sampling time unavailable.
assertions.quantitative_result: YRI/ESN CC12 AC11 AA2; IBS CC12 AC12 AA3; percentages source-reported approximate

assertions.subject: chr21q22 1.85-kb enhancer CRISPR deletion
assertions.source_locator: Fig1e,f; Results Resolving molecular mechanisms at chr21q22; Methods monocyte differentiation, CRISPR editing and PrimeFlow; selected L303,309,391–399
assertions.evidence_summary: Enhancer deletion reduced ETS2 RNA upregulation during inflammatory differentiation; BRWD1 and PSMG1 RNA were unaffected. PrimeFlow measured RNA, because candidate-gene flow protein antibodies were unavailable.
assertions.dose: GM-CSF50 ng/mL;TNF50 ng/mL;PGE2 1 microgram/mL;Pam3CSK4 1 microgram/mL;RNP into5 million monocytes in100 microlitre buffer
assertions.assay: PrimeFlow ETS2 AlexaFluor647;BRWD1/PSMG1 AlexaFluor568;PCR/Bioanalyzer deletion confirmation
assertions.causal_directness: Direct enhancer-region perturbation with target RNA measurement; not exact variant replacement.
assertions.limitations: Incomplete deletion; no native ETS2 protein readout in this arm; no rescue assigning all enhancer functional effects exclusively to ETS2; donor overlap with downstream panels unavailable.
assertions.quantitative_result: Fig1f n=4 donors; effect size unavailable. Mean enhancer editing42.4% across broader n=11 editing panel, not assigned to n4 as individual efficiency.

assertions.subject: ETS2 CRISPR coding-exon disruption
assertions.source_locator: Fig2b; Results Macrophage inflammation requires ETS2; Methods CRISPR editing and Cytokine quantification; selected L325,328,395–396,415–416
assertions.evidence_summary: ETS2 disruption reduced IL6 protein measured in inflammatory macrophage supernatant. Two guides target different ETS2 exons; cytokine concentrations were measured by electrochemiluminescence in duplicate.
assertions.dose: GM-CSF50 ng/mL;TNF50 ng/mL;PGE2 1 microgram/mL;Pam3CSK4 1 microgram/mL;RNP into5 million monocytes in100 microlitre buffer
assertions.assay: Meso Scale Diagnostics electrochemiluminescence; DISCOVERY WORKBENCH4.0
assertions.time_point: supernatant collected day6 of TPP macrophage culture
assertions.causal_directness: Direct gene disruption with measured extracellular protein endpoint.
assertions.limitations: Editing verified at DNA and reduced expression by RNA, not native ETS2 protein abundance in this arm. IL10 was less affected, and TNF was not assessed because added exogenously. Viability/marker controls in separate panels unaffected; donor overlaps unavailable.
assertions.quantitative_result: Fig2b n=8; numerical IL6 effect unavailable. Broader editing panels approximately89.7%/78.6% for guides1/2, not assumed per cytokine sample.

assertions.subject: ETS2 CRISPR coding-exon disruption
assertions.source_locator: Fig2c; Results Macrophage inflammation requires ETS2; Methods Phagocytosis; selected L325,328,417–418
assertions.evidence_summary: ETS2-disrupted macrophages had reduced uptake-based phagocytosis index for fluorescent zymosan compared with non-targeting controls.
assertions.dose: GM-CSF50 ng/mL;TNF50 ng/mL;PGE2 1 microgram/mL;Pam3CSK4 1 microgram/mL;RNP into5 million monocytes in100 microlitre buffer

assertions.dose: GM-CSF50 ng/mL;TNF50 ng/mL;PGE2 1 microgram/mL;Pam3CSK4 1 microgram/mL;RNP into5 million monocytes in100 microlitre buffer
assertions.assay: Green Zymosan flow cytometry;index=positive fraction times positive-cell MFI;100000 cells/well;cytochalasinD10 microgram/mL negative control

synthesis: Human immune regulatory mechanisms are represented as context-specific perturbational links and branches. DDX39B depletion/rescue supports a narrow HeLa splicing mechanism. Activated primary CD4 cells provide shared-intervention RNA/supernatant evidence with discordant shRNAs and non-isoform-specific ELISA. Primary-cell CD81 promoter repression supplies RNA and measured surface-protein branches. Enhancer-to-TRAF1 and KCNN4 results broaden regulatory scope without inferring protein or disease causality. No review, priors, or release changes performed. ETS2 source access was subsequently resolved: four bounded primary-macrophage assertions provide enhancer→RNA/function and ETS2 disruption→IL6 protein/function branches, with no forced native-protein mediation.
